q: The trimming shop of a carriage workshop is primarily concerned with:

options.A: Repair of coach bogies
options.B: Painting of coach exteriors
options.C: Furnishing work of coaches, such as cushions, curtains and rexine or leather work
options.D: Manufacture of springs for coaches

q: In a workshop, the inspection of a manufactured or repaired article is not entrusted to the shop which produced it, but is kept organisationally separate from the producing shop. This separation is maintained mainly so that:

options.A: The producing shop can start the next job earlier
options.B: The stores depot can take the article into stock without a receipt note
options.C: The inspection staff can also fix the allowed times for the job
options.D: The inspection remains independent and impartial, and defective work is not passed by those who produced it

q: While checking the stores requisitions of a manufacture job, the Workshop Accounts Office compares the drawals of material with the bill of materials (material schedule) prepared for the job. The main object of this comparison is to ensure that:

options.A: Material is not drawn in excess of the requirements of the job
options.B: The job is completed before the end of the financial year
options.C: The stores depot maintains its bin cards correctly
options.D: The workers on the job earn the maximum incentive bonus

q: The turning of wheel tyres to profile and the mounting and pressing of wheels on axles in a workshop is carried out in the:

options.A: Erecting shop
options.B: Wheel shop
options.C: Smithy
options.D: Paint shop

q: Before a workpiece is machined or fabricated, a fitter performs the operation of marking out (layout) on it. Marking out consists of:

options.A: Painting the workpiece in the shop colour
options.B: Weighing the workpiece and entering it in the Plant Register
options.C: Scribing the lines, dimensions and centre points on the workpiece which guide the subsequent machining or fabrication
options.D: Testing the hardness of the workpiece

q: Final assembly or erection of locomotives or coaches and their major components in a workshop is carried out in the:

options.A: Foundry
options.B: Pattern shop
options.C: Stores depot
options.D: Erecting shop

q: Painting, varnishing and finishing or lining of coaches, wagons and components in a workshop is the work of the:

options.A: Paint shop
options.B: Millwright shop
options.C: Electrical shop
options.D: Tool room

q: Forging work, that is, shaping heated metal for the manufacture and repair of components in a workshop, is carried out principally in the:

options.A: Carpentry shop
options.B: Smithy
options.C: Foundry
options.D: Wheel shop

q: Stores received into the depot attached to a workshop remain in the custody and accountal of the stores depot up to the point at which they are:

options.A: Consumed on a job in the shop
options.B: Entered in the Workshop General Register
options.C: Issued to a shop against an authorised requisition quoting the work order
options.D: Verified by the stock verifier at the annual verification

q: Repairs to the electrical equipment of coaches, such as fans, lights and dynamos or batteries, are carried out in a workshop in the:

options.A: Paint shop
options.B: Millwright shop
options.C: Tool room
options.D: Electrical shop

q: The Golden Rock Railway Workshop, a major repair workshop of the Southern Railway, is located at:

options.A: Tiruchirappalli
options.B: Jamalpur
options.C: Kharagpur
options.D: Matunga, Mumbai

q: The Jamalpur Workshop of the Eastern Railway is situated in the State of:

options.A: West Bengal
options.B: Bihar
options.C: Jharkhand
options.D: Uttar Pradesh

q: The Rail Wheel Plant at Bela in Bihar is a production unit engaged in the manufacture of:

options.A: Locomotives
options.B: Passenger coaches
options.C: Wheels for rolling stock
options.D: Rails and sleepers

q: The Rail Spring Karkhana at Sithouli, near Gwalior, is a production unit which manufactures:

options.A: Wheels and axles
options.B: Electric locomotives
options.C: Signalling cables
options.D: Springs for rolling stock

q: On the executive side, a railway workshop is headed by the:

options.A: Chief Workshop Manager
options.B: Workshop Accounts Officer
options.C: Controller of Stores
options.D: Travelling Inspector of Accounts

q: During a year's working, a workshop opens with work-in-progress, books expenditure on jobs during the year and transfers out its completed outturn. Which of the following equations correctly reconciles the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense of the workshop for the year?

options.A: Opening work-in-progress + expenditure booked during the year = outturn transferred out + closing work-in-progress
options.B: Opening work-in-progress + outturn transferred out = expenditure booked during the year + closing work-in-progress
options.C: Expenditure booked during the year = closing work-in-progress only
options.D: Outturn transferred out = opening work-in-progress only

q: The Workshop Accounts Officer is checking the monthly outturn statement of the workshop before its submission. Part I of that statement is meant to show:

options.A: The outlay, that is, the money spent on the jobs of each shop
options.B: The outturn, that is, the work done and completed by each shop
options.C: The on-cost percentages worked out for the workshop
options.D: The closing balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense

q: When a manufacture job in a workshop is finished, a completion report is drawn up for the job primarily in order to:

options.A: Fix the pay of the staff who were engaged on the job
options.B: Close the workshop accounts for the month
options.C: Record the final cost of the job and compare it with the sanctioned estimate for the job
options.D: Revise the stores price ledger of the depot

q: Before charges against a job can be watched in accounts, the work order authorising the job must invariably state:

options.A: The name of the worker who will execute the job
options.B: The market price expected for the finished article
options.C: The date of the next periodic overhaul of the workshop
options.D: The head of account or allocation to which the cost of the job is chargeable

q: A work order has been closed after completion of the job and transfer of its outturn. A shop thereafter seeks to book a small material charge to that work order. The correct position is that:

options.A: Charges may be booked to it till the end of the financial year
options.B: No further expenditure can be booked to that work order
options.C: Only material charges can be booked to it thereafter
options.D: Only labour charges can be booked to it thereafter

q: Material issued from the stores depot for execution of a workshop job is priced, for debiting the job, at:

options.A: The latest market rate ruling on the date of issue
options.B: The rate at which the material was originally manufactured
options.C: The stores price-ledger (issue) rate
options.D: A rate fixed by the shop incharge for the job

q: Material required for a workshop job is drawn from the stores depot only against:

options.A: A verbal demand made by the worker on the job
options.B: The route card of the job, without any requisition
options.C: The completion report of the previous job of the shop
options.D: An authorised requisition (issue note) quoting the work order of the job

q: The cost of special tools and jigs which are consumed on one particular manufacture job is treated in workshop costing as:

options.A: A charge on that job itself
options.B: A part of the shop on-cost of the shop
options.C: A part of the general on-cost of the workshop
options.D: A proforma charge spread over all jobs

q: Material is purchased specifically for one particular job and is not taken into depot stock. Its cost is:

options.A: Held under Stores Suspense till the job is completed
options.B: Charged directly to the work order of that job
options.C: Charged to the shop on-cost of the shop executing the job
options.D: First taken into stock and only then issued to the job

q: Material drawn for a job is later found surplus and is returned to the stores depot. The job is credited for the returned material at:

options.A: The current market price on the date of return
options.B: Half of the price at which it was issued
options.C: A price fixed by the shop incharge
options.D: The same price at which the material was issued to the job

q:
Consider the following statements about reconciliation of a workshop worker's time:
1. The time booked by the worker on job cards and tally sheets, together with his recorded idle time, should account for his total attendance time as per the gate or time cards.
2. Differences between the attendance time and the booked time which remain unaccounted for are investigated by the Accounts office.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The periodical review of the Workshop General Register by the Workshop Accounts Officer is undertaken mainly in order to:

options.A: Detect jobs lying incomplete or outstanding for long periods and secure their early clearance
options.B: Fix the pay of the workshop staff
options.C: Prepare the annual budget of the Railway
options.D: Verify the cash balance of the workshop cash office

q: The aggregate cost of the jobs in progress, as compiled job-wise in the Workshop General Register, should agree with:

options.A: The balance under Stores Suspense in the general books
options.B: The balance under Traffic Suspense in the general books
options.C: The balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense in the general books
options.D: The balance of the shop on-cost account of the workshop

q: A copy of every work order issued in a workshop is sent to the Workshop Accounts Office chiefly so that:

options.A: It can purchase the material required for the job
options.B: The charges booked against the work order can be watched and the cost of the job compiled in the Workshop General Register
options.C: It can fix the wages of the staff who will work on the job
options.D: It can sell the finished articles of the job

q: Standing work orders in a workshop, against which routine repetitive work is booked, are distinguished by the fact that they bear:

options.A: A fresh number allotted on every occasion of use
options.B: Numbers allotted by the Railway Board for each separate item of work
options.C: No number at all, being identified only by the name of the shop
options.D: Fixed numbers allotted to specified classes of routine or repetitive work, charges being booked against them as and when such work is done

q: Standard components are manufactured in a batch under a single batch work order. The cost per article of the batch is arrived at by:

options.A: Dividing the total cost of the batch by the number of articles produced in the batch
options.B: Dividing the direct labour cost of the batch by the number of articles
options.C: Dividing the total cost of the batch by the number of work orders issued
options.D: Adopting the market price of a similar article

q: For judging the economy of overhaul work, the total Periodic Overhaul outlay of a workshop for a period is expressed as a unit cost by dividing it by:

options.A: The number of shops in the workshop
options.B: The total staff strength of the workshop
options.C: The number of units turned out in the period
options.D: The number of units programmed for overhaul in the next year

q: The prime cost built up on a workshop manufacture job consists of:

options.A: Direct material and shop on-cost only
options.B: Direct material, direct labour and direct expenses chargeable to the job
options.C: Direct labour and general on-cost only
options.D: All costs of the job, including proforma on-cost

q: In a workshop cost sheet, the works cost, also called the shop cost, of a job is arrived at as:

options.A: Prime cost plus general on-cost and proforma on-cost
options.B: Direct material cost alone
options.C: Prime cost plus proforma on-cost only
options.D: Prime cost plus shop on-cost

q: A workshop has compiled the prime cost, shop on-cost and general on-cost of an article it manufactures. To state the article's full cost, proforma on-cost is further added to:

options.A: The prime cost plus shop on-cost and general on-cost
options.B: The direct labour cost alone
options.C: The direct material cost alone
options.D: The selling price of the article

q: On-cost has been absorbed on jobs at predetermined rates, but the actual on-cost incurred for the period turns out to be different. The difference between the on-cost so absorbed and the actual on-cost is known as:

options.A: Work-in-progress
options.B: Suspense balance
options.C: Over-absorption or under-absorption of on-cost
options.D: Departmental charges

q: The on-cost rates in force in a workshop are required to be revised when:

options.A: A new Workshop Accounts Officer assumes charge of the workshop
options.B: The actual on-cost incurred differs widely and persistently from the on-cost absorbed on jobs
options.C: The workshop changes its weekly holiday
options.D: A new shop is added to the workshop

q: The shop on-cost percentage to be applied to the jobs of a shop is worked out as:

options.A: Total shop on-cost divided by the total material cost of the shop
options.B: Total direct labour of the shop divided by the total shop on-cost
options.C: Total shop on-cost divided by the number of jobs done in the shop
options.D: Total shop on-cost divided by the total direct labour charges of the shop, expressed as a percentage

q: In a shop where the work is predominantly machine-based, the on-cost of the shop may be absorbed on its jobs on the basis of:

options.A: The machine hours worked on the jobs, through a machine-hour rate
options.B: The direct material cost of the jobs
options.C: The number of workers present in the shop
options.D: The floor area occupied by each job

q: In booking the wages of apprentices under training in a workshop, the correct routing in workshop costing is that:

options.A: The wages of all apprentices are booked directly to the jobs on which they practise
options.B: The wages of all apprentices are treated as a proforma charge on jobs
options.C: The wages of apprentices attached to a particular shop are charged to the shop on-cost of that shop, while those of apprentices not attached to any shop are charged to general on-cost
options.D: The wages of all apprentices are charged to the Capital head of the workshop

q: While costing the outturn of a workshop, the stipend paid to a trade apprentice who is still under training and whose time is not booked to any individual job is treated as:

options.A: Direct wages of the jobs on which the apprentice practises
options.B: An on-cost charge, since the apprentice is a trainee and his stipend is not booked to individual jobs
options.C: A loan recoverable from the apprentice after training
options.D: A part of the material cost of the jobs of the shop

q: The labour pay sheets of a workshop are prepared by the Accounts office from the time and tally sheets rendered by the shops. In the internal check of these pay sheets, the Accounts office ensures, among other things, that:

options.A: All workers of the workshop are paid only in cash
options.B: The outturn of the shop exceeds the programme for the month
options.C: The material issues to the shop are within the Average Annual Consumption
options.D: The time booked to jobs agrees with the job cards and tally sheets

q: The idle time of workshop staff is brought on record primarily through:

options.A: Idle time cards or statements showing the period and the reasons for the idleness, certified by the shop supervision
options.B: Completion reports of the jobs of the shop
options.C: Route cards of the jobs in progress
options.D: Material requisitions issued by the shop

q: A worker under the incentive scheme loses time on account of a failure of power, a cause beyond his control, and the period is duly recorded as idle time. For that idle period, the worker:

options.A: Earns bonus at the average rate of the shop
options.B: Is paid no wages at all
options.C: Is paid wages at the time rate, but earns no bonus on that period
options.D: Is treated as being on leave without pay

q: The wages of direct workers of a workshop for periods of authorised leave, which cannot be booked to any particular job, are charged to:

options.A: A capital work order of the workshop
options.B: Shop on-cost
options.C: The next job undertaken by the worker
options.D: Stores Suspense

q: Royalty paid by a workshop for the use of a patented process employed exclusively on one particular manufacture job is treated in workshop costing as:

options.A: A direct expense of that job, charged to its work order as part of its prime cost
options.B: A part of the general on-cost of the workshop as a whole
options.C: A proforma charge notionally added to all jobs of the workshop
options.D: A deduction from the sale value of the article manufactured

q: Where two or more products of substantial value are produced simultaneously from the same material and process in a workshop, the common (joint) cost incurred up to the point at which the products become separately identifiable is generally apportioned among the joint products on the basis of:

options.A: The number of workers employed on each product
options.B: The sales value of each product at the split-off point
options.C: The floor area occupied in producing each product
options.D: The direct wages booked on each product after the split-off point

q: In costing the outturn of a workshop, the amount realised from the sale of a by-product of a job or process is generally dealt with by:

options.A: Adding it to the cost of the main product of the job
options.B: Crediting it to the general on-cost account of the workshop
options.C: Crediting it to the account of the job or process, so that the cost of the main product is reduced to that extent
options.D: Treating it as a part of the wages fund of the shop

q: The wages paid to workshop workers for abnormal idle time, that is, idle time arising from abnormal causes such as a major breakdown of machinery or prolonged failure of power, are treated in cost accounts by:

options.A: Charging them to the job on which the workers were last engaged
options.B: Spreading them over all the jobs of the shop as shop on-cost
options.C: Adding them to the material cost of the jobs in hand
options.D: Excluding them from the cost of production and charging them to the Costing Profit and Loss Account

q: Under SDE analysis, as applied to the items of material held for workshop use, the items are classified according to:

options.A: Their availability for procurement, that is, whether an item is scarce, difficult to obtain, or easy to obtain
options.B: Their annual consumption value
options.C: Their unit price, whether high, medium or low
options.D: Their rate of movement, whether fast, slow or non-moving

q: For unit-wise compilation of the cost of Periodic Overhaul in a repair workshop, the arrangement followed is that:

options.A: One common work order is used for all units overhauled in a year
options.B: The overhaul cost is compiled shop-wise and never unit-wise
options.C: Units are grouped class-wise under a single work order for the whole year
options.D: A distinct work order is allotted to each unit of rolling stock taken up for overhaul

q: Every item of machinery and plant installed in a workshop is recorded, with its cost and particulars, in the Plant Register, where the item is identified by:

options.A: A distinctive plant number allotted to each machine
options.B: The token number of the worker operating the machine
options.C: The price-ledger number of the stores depot
options.D: The number of the work order on which it was installed

q: When an item of machinery and plant is transferred from one workshop to another workshop, the correct treatment is that:

options.A: The transaction is ignored in the accounts of both workshops
options.B: The receiving workshop treats the machine as a free gift with no accountal
options.C: Corresponding adjustments are made in the Plant Registers and accounts of the transferring and receiving units
options.D: The cost of the machine is written off to the revenue of the transferring workshop

q: A machine in a workshop which has gone beyond economical repair is dealt with by:

options.A: Keeping it in the Plant Register permanently at its full original value
options.B: Condemning it under the orders of the competent authority and removing it from the Plant Register
options.C: Transferring it to the stores depot as serviceable stock
options.D: Charging its full original cost to the shop on-cost of the shop

q: The cost of work done by a railway workshop for another railway is recovered:

options.A: In cash from the cash office of the other railway's workshop
options.B: By debiting the cost finally to the home railway's revenue head
options.C: By adjustment against stores supplied by that railway, in all cases
options.D: Through transfer transactions (Account Current) between the accounts offices of the two railways

q: A workshop takes up and executes a job on behalf of another Government department. The amount charged to that department for the job is:

options.A: Cost plus the prescribed departmental charges
options.B: Cost only, with no addition of any kind
options.C: Double the cost of the job
options.D: A nominal charge of one rupee per job

q:
Consider the following statements about incentive payment in a workshop:
1. The allowed time for a job is fixed by the rate fixer on the basis of time studies (work measurement).
2. Bonus under the incentive scheme is payable only on measured jobs for which allowed times have been fixed.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A measured job is executed jointly by a gang of workers under the incentive scheme. The bonus earned on the job is distributed among the members of the gang:

options.A: Equally among all members, irrespective of their wages
options.B: In proportion to the time wages of each member
options.C: To the gang leader alone, who distributes it at his discretion
options.D: In proportion to the seniority of the members

q: Essential indirect workers attached to a shop, such as helpers and crane operators, whose individual output cannot be measured, are paid incentive bonus:

options.A: At a flat rate fixed by the shop incharge
options.B: Only when the shop completes its annual programme
options.C: At double the rate earned by the direct workers
options.D: Linked to the average bonus earned by the direct workers of the shop

q: Under the Group Incentive Scheme in a workshop, the incentive payable to a group is computed on the basis of:

options.A: Only such outturn as is passed and accepted
options.B: All outturn, including rejected work
options.C: The attendance of the group members alone
options.D: The savings in material cost alone

q: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is described as a suspense head mainly because:

options.A: Its balance is withheld from audit scrutiny
options.B: Expenditure is first collected on jobs without final allocation, the final head being determined on completion and transfer of the outturn
options.C: Every item booked under it is of a doubtful nature
options.D: It is opened only at the close of the financial year

q: A shop draws material well in advance for jobs that have not yet been taken in hand. The immediate accounting effect of such advance drawal is that:

options.A: The balance under Stores Suspense alone increases
options.B: The balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense decreases
options.C: The balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense increases without any corresponding outturn, the material remaining charged to jobs not yet executed
options.D: There is no effect on the balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense

q: Jobs in a shop stand physically completed and completion reports have been received, but the transfer entries for the outturn remain unpassed for several months. The result of this delay is that:

options.A: The balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense remains inflated even though the work itself has been completed
options.B: The work orders concerned stand closed automatically
options.C: The balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is reduced without any accounting entry
options.D: The accumulated cost of the jobs is transferred to shop on-cost

q: The balance under Stores Suspense is distinguished from the balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense in that Stores Suspense represents:

options.A: The value of jobs in progress in workshops
options.B: The arrears of wages of stores depot staff
options.C: The value of scrap awaiting disposal in depots
options.D: The value of stores stock held in depots, whereas Workshop Manufacturing Suspense represents the value of jobs in progress in workshops

q: In workshop accounts, the total credits arising on the transfer of completed work are known as:

options.A: Earnings
options.B: Receipts
options.C: Outturn, the total debits booked to jobs during the period being known as outlay
options.D: Appropriation

q: Direct labour charges are adopted as the main basis for distributing on-cost over workshop jobs because:

options.A: Most indirect expenses of a shop are related to the labour employed and the time worked on jobs
options.B: The material cost of jobs cannot be ascertained in a workshop
options.C: Direct labour is the only cost incurred in a workshop
options.D: This basis is prescribed in the Stores Code

q: A clerk who keeps the records of a single shop and is not booked to any individual job is paid from wages that are treated in workshop costing as:

options.A: Direct labour of the jobs done in that shop
options.B: Indirect labour charged to the shop on-cost of that shop
options.C: Proforma on-cost of the workshop
options.D: General on-cost of the workshop

q: The gate time office of a workshop serves every shop in recording the attendance of staff. Its cost is accordingly borne in workshop costing as:

options.A: General on-cost, since the time office serves the workshop as a whole
options.B: Shop on-cost of the erecting shop only
options.C: A direct charge on the first job taken up each day
options.D: Proforma on-cost of the workshop

q: Proforma on-cost of a workshop includes which of the following notional charges?

options.A: Power consumed by the machines of a shop
options.B: Wages of the foreman of a shop
options.C: Pension contribution in respect of workshop staff, charged notionally
options.D: Consumable stores used in a shop

q:
Consider the following statements about the timing of cost ascertainment:
1. Under job costing, the cost of a job becomes known when the job is completed.
2. Under process costing, the unit cost is worked out for a period by dividing the cost of the process for that period by its output.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Job cards, material requisitions and completion reports of a job all quote the number of its work order. This quoting serves mainly to ensure that:

options.A: All labour, material and on-cost relating to the job can be linked and accumulated under that work order
options.B: The stores depot can fix the issue price of material
options.C: The pay of the workers on the job can be fixed
options.D: The job can be identified by the audit party

q: Besides the classification by head of account, workshop work orders fall, by the nature of the work covered, into the two broad classes of:

options.A: Audited work orders and unaudited work orders
options.B: Cash work orders and credit work orders
options.C: Local work orders and foreign work orders only
options.D: Manufacture work orders and repair work orders

q: Month after month, the same routine oiling and servicing of shop machinery is carried out in a workshop. Such recurring work is charged in workshop accounts to:

options.A: A fresh specific work order issued every month
options.B: The same Revenue Standing Work Order allotted for such routine work
options.C: The Capital head of the workshop
options.D: Stores Suspense

q: A special fixture is needed once only, for one particular capital work. Its manufacture in the workshop should be executed under:

options.A: A Revenue Standing Work Order
options.B: A specific work order issued for that job
options.C: The on-cost standing work order of the shop
options.D: No work order at all

q: Besides showing the sequence of operations of a job, the route card serves during the execution of the job to:

options.A: Record the completion of each operation by the shop concerned as the job moves from shop to shop
options.B: Fix the wages payable to the workers on the job
options.C: Price the material issued to the job
options.D: Close the work order on completion of the job

q: The route card of a job is not the same document as its job card, because the route card:

options.A: Records the attendance of the worker at the workshop gate
options.B: Is the document on the basis of which wages are paid
options.C: Prescribes the operations and the shops through which the job will pass, whereas the job card records the time spent by a worker on the job
options.D: Shows the material to be purchased for the job

q: At the workshop gate, the time keeper compiles the time book of the workshop from:

options.A: The labour pay sheets of the workshop
options.B: The route cards of the jobs in progress
options.C: The stores issue notes of the depot
options.D: The gate attendance (clock) cards of the workers

q: From the gate and time records, a workshop prepares an absentee statement. Such a statement brings out:

options.A: The machines which remained idle during the day
options.B: The workers absent or on leave during the period, so that their pay can be regulated in the pay sheets
options.C: The material not issued by the stores depot
options.D: The jobs remaining incomplete in the shop

q: For compiling the monthly Workshop Outturn Statement, the Workshop Accounts Office relies mainly on:

options.A: The completion reports and shop returns of outturn and expenditure
options.B: The stores price ledger maintained in the depot
options.C: The cash book of the workshop cash office
options.D: The muster rolls of casual labour

q: Part I and Part II of the Workshop Outturn Statement are agreed with each other because a disagreement between the quantity of outturn and the outlay points to:

options.A: Excess staff posted in the shop
options.B: Wrong pricing of stores in the price ledger
options.C: Shortage of material in the stores depot
options.D: Jobs shown as completed but not transferred out, or expenditure booked on jobs not shown as completed

q: A workshop, being a separate accounting unit, renders its Account Current to the headquarters accounts office of the railway in order that:

options.A: The transactions of the workshop are incorporated in the general books of the railway
options.B: Audited directly by the C&AG
options.C: Published in the Works Programme (Pink Book)
options.D: Compared with the Traffic Book of the railway

q: For work done by a workshop for other accounting units, the entry made in the workshop's Account Current is:

options.A: A credit in favour of those units
options.B: A debit against those units, and work done for the workshop by other units as a credit
options.C: A suspense item, without debit or credit
options.D: An item of shop on-cost of the workshop

q: Railways obtain the rolling stock provided under the Rolling Stock Programme by:

options.A: Purchase from passengers and the public
options.B: Transfer from the stores depot only
options.C: Manufacture in railway workshops and production units or purchase from trade, as decided for each item
options.D: Hire from other Government departments only

q: In scope, the Machinery and Plant Programme is wider than a programme confined to workshops, because it covers plant and machinery required:

options.A: Only for locomotive workshops
options.B: Only for the Railway Board's office
options.C: Only for production units manufacturing locomotives
options.D: For workshops, sheds, depots and other units across the railway, and not merely for workshops alone

q: For the year, the itemised works sanctioned under the Rolling Stock Programme and the Machinery and Plant Programme find a place in the railway's:

options.A: Traffic Book
options.B: Works Programme (Pink Book)
options.C: Stores Budget only
options.D: Appropriation Accounts

q: In the CLW pattern incentive scheme, the bonus of a worker who saves time on a job is paid on:

options.A: The full value of the time saved, his earnings being worked out on the allowed time for the job
options.B: 50 per cent of the value of the time saved only
options.C: 30 per cent of the value of the time saved only
options.D: The time taken by him only, with no bonus at all

q: Under the Group Incentive Scheme, the incentive of every member of a group moves with the outturn of the group as a whole, in that:

options.A: A shortfall in the outturn of the group reduces the incentive payable to all its members
options.B: Each member's bonus depends only on his individual output
options.C: The absence of a member has no effect on the group
options.D: Bonus is payable even if the group turns out no work

q: The working programme of a repair workshop is centred mainly on:

options.A: The same production programme of new rolling stock
options.B: The Machinery and Plant Programme of the railway
options.C: A programme of manufacture of stores items only
options.D: A Periodic Overhaul programme based on the arisings of stock due for overhaul

q: Work-in-progress has to be valued at the close of a period in a process shop because, in such a shop:

options.A: All jobs in a process shop are completed every day
options.B: Partly processed units remain in the process at the close of the period and their cost must be separated from the cost of the completed output
options.C: Process shops are not required to maintain cost records
options.D: The outturn of a process shop is transferred out only once a year

q: PU 35 of the home railway is not charged with the material used in overhauling, in its workshop, rolling stock belonging to another railway, for the reason that:

options.A: PU 35 covers labour charges and not material
options.B: Foreign rolling stock is overhauled free of cost
options.C: The material for such overhaul is supplied by the passengers
options.D: The cost of such overhaul is recoverable from the owning railway and is not a final charge on the home railway

q: A supplementary rate in workshop costing is used for the purpose of:

options.A: Fix the selling price of an article manufactured in the workshop for an outside party
options.B: Recover the direct material cost of a job in advance of its completion
options.C: Distribute the difference between the overhead absorbed and the overhead actually incurred over the jobs of the period
options.D: Replace the predetermined absorption rate for all jobs of the following year

q: Material issued from a workshop store is priced on the first-in-first-out method when the issue is valued at:

options.A: The price of the most recent lot of the material received into the store
options.B: The average price of all the lots of the material in stock
options.C: The price of the earliest lot of the material still in stock, lots being exhausted in the order in which they were received
options.D: The price at which the material could be replaced in the market on the date of issue

q: Material issued from a workshop store is priced on the last-in-first-out method when the issue is valued at:

options.A: The price of the most recent lot of the material received, that lot being treated as issued first
options.B: The price of the earliest lot of the material received into the store
options.C: The standard price fixed for the material for the whole year
options.D: The lowest price at which the material was received during the year

q: Service departments of a workshop render services to each other as well as to production departments. Their costs are reapportioned on the reciprocal method when:

options.A: Each service department is apportioned to the production departments one after another, without recognising the services it receives from other service departments
options.B: The costs of all service departments are charged wholly to the largest production department
options.C: No service department cost is apportioned to any production department at all
options.D: The services rendered by one service department to another are recognised, the departments being treated as rendering services to each other mutually

q: In XYZ analysis of material held for workshop use, classification of the items is made according to:

options.A: The unit price of the items, from the highest-priced to the lowest-priced
options.B: The value of the stock of each item held in store, the items of highest stock value forming the X class, those of medium stock value the Y class and those of lowest stock value the Z class
options.C: The annual value of consumption of the items
options.D: The source from which the items are procured, whether local or foreign

q: A workshop store follows continuous stock taking when:

options.A: The entire store is closed once a year and every item in it is counted at one time
options.B: Only the items suspected of shortage are counted, and that too only on a complaint
options.C: A few items are counted and checked in rotation every day throughout the year, so that each item is verified several times without closing the store
options.D: The stock is verified only when the storekeeper in charge of the store is transferred

q: A worker books time on a job whose work order already stands closed and whose outturn has been transferred. Such booking is objectionable chiefly because:

options.A: Closed work orders earn incentive bonus for the shop
options.B: It reduces the wages payable to the worker for that day
options.C: It increases the balance under Stores Suspense
options.D: It reopens a completed cost, distorts the transferred cost of the outturn and points to defective time booking in the shop

q: In a shop, material drawn for one job is actually consumed on another job. For each job to bear the cost of the material actually used on it, the booking is regularised by:

options.A: Ignoring the diversion, since both jobs belong to the same shop
options.B: Charging the material a second time to the second job, without crediting the first
options.C: Returning the material physically to the depot in every case, even after consumption
options.D: Passing a transfer between the two work orders, so that each job bears the material actually consumed on it

q: An idle time card or statement is required to support the idle time recorded for a worker in a shop chiefly so that:

options.A: The worker can be fined for every hour of idleness
options.B: The stores depot can price the material issued to the shop
options.C: The causes of idleness can be analysed and responsibility fixed, and the wages for the idle period can be dealt with correctly in costing
options.D: The outturn of the shop can be transferred to Stores

q: In the time booking of a workshop worker, his overtime hours are shown separately from his normal hours chiefly because:

options.A: The extra payment for overtime has to be computed and its incidence in costing, on the job or on on-cost, has to be decided
options.B: Overtime hours are not recorded on the gate cards at all
options.C: The wages for the overtime hours are never paid to the worker
options.D: Overtime work is always executed under a separate work order
